exposure: Respiratory Severity Score (RSS) on the first day of life (categorized as <2, 2-5, >5)
outcome: Respiratory morbidity (respiratory support after 36 weeks postmenstrual age)
Neurologic morbidity (periventricular leukomalacia or high-grade intraventricular hemorrhage)
cohort: The study included 730 premature inborn infants born between 400 and 1250 g, whose data were extracted from the NYS Perinatal Data System from 2006 to 2016.
finding: Higher Respiratory Severity Score (RSS ≥2) on the first day of life is associated with an increased risk of mortality and morbidities (respiratory, neurologic, severe) in infants born ≤ 1250 g.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery did not differ by Respiratory Severity Score (RSS) category.
followup_time: At least until 36 weeks postmenstrual age for respiratory morbidity, and unspecified for other outcomes like mortality (likely hospital discharge or defined early infant period).
